| [0010](./0010/) | core | accepted | major | not-started | 2026-08-07 — Slice `core-platform-and-match` landed in `core`, implementing D14, D28, D32, D36 and D37 — the third of the four slices in the unpublished alpha, leaving 0011's `core-identity-package` before `core-alpha-release` can cut. SELECTION: the subscription filter definition is deleted outright and `#Subscription` carries a required scalar `version!`, so catalog selection is a pure function of committed source — git-identical inputs materialize identical bytes with no lockfile, because the platform file IS the resolution. Two builds of one catalog is two platforms, and the map key makes the alternative a conflict rather than a discouraged shape. MATCHING: `matchLabels` lands on `#Resource`, `#Trait`, `#Blueprint` and `#Component`, unified WHOLESALE with no filter; `#ComponentTransformer.requiredLabels` selects on it; `metadata.labels` keeps categorisation and is never unified upward; `#LabelWorkloadType` is deleted, so `core` names no matching key. TWO CLAIMS WERE DELETED RATHER THAN CORRECTED, and this is the one finding that changes the story: `metadata.labels` was documented as unified from every attached primitive in BOTH the schema comment and SPEC.md, and NOTHING PERFORMED THAT UNION — not the CUE, and not the kernel, which reads `metadata.labels` off the component value at `compile/match.go:111`. What made label matching work was catalogs writing the label onto a component FRAGMENT by hand, which is exactly what D36 removes. FULFILMENT: `fulfilment: *"catalog" | "provider"` on `#Resource` and `#Trait` only; `#Blueprint` is excluded structurally and a declaration there is `field not allowed`. D28 SPELLING, which this slice was left to pick: the trait opt-out is a MARKER SET on `#Component` — `#optionalTraits?: [#ContractFQNType]: true` — keyed by the same contract FQN the `#traits` map is keyed by, with no `false`, so absence is the only spelling of required. A field on `#Trait` was rejected as supply-side; a second attachment map was rejected because catalogs ship fragments that attach into `#traits` and a module author cannot move where a fragment put a trait, while a marker is writable beside one; a list was rejected because two fragments unifying into one component fail on list unification while map keys merge. Resources get no marker, per D28. TWO CONSEQUENCES SHIP HERE RATHER THAN LATER: rendered objects stop carrying `core.opmodel.dev/workload-type`, because `matchLabels` is deliberately not folded into `#TransformerContext` (recorded at the fold site, since the omission otherwise reads as an oversight); and every live Platform with a range must be rewritten to a scalar `version`, which is cluster work outside both entries. `src/platform_and_match_pins.cue` pins the properties, with seven MUST-FAIL cases measured in place against cue v0.17.1. TWO OF THOSE ARE MISSING REQUIRED FIELDS, which `cue vet` does not report: the unanswered match-label case surfaces under an ordinary `cue export` because `matchLabels` is a REGULAR field, while the version-less subscription does NOT, because `#registry` is hidden and even concrete evaluation skips it — the field has to be named, which is what a kernel does. THE LIBRARY STILL READS `metadata.labels` FOR MATCHING: shipping this schema without `library-match-labels` leaves a matcher that silently matches nothing, so a green `task check` in `core` is not evidence the system works end to end. NOT PUBLISHED — `core-alpha-release` remains the cut point. | Module and Catalog Identity |
| [0011](./0011/) | cli | accepted | minor | not-started | 2026-08-05 — `plan.yaml` gains a structured `decisions` field and the repo gains `task decisions:uncovered`. MEASURED FIRST, because the trigger was a cap firing and the useful question was whether the cap was wrong: across the 27 slices in the two entries with plans, the median `concern` sat at 205 of its 240-rune limit, 15 of 27 were within 40 runes, and up to 41 runes went on an inline decision-citation tail (0011's cli-publish-pipeline, 11 decisions). So the cap was not being abused — it had no headroom, and the pressure was ONE-DIRECTIONAL, since a slice's citation list accretes while its description does not. Nothing parsed those citations. RAISING THE CAP WAS REJECTED as treating the symptom and re-arming it later; the field was carrying two things, a one-line description and a decision index, and only the first is what the thinness rule is about. THE COVERAGE INVERSE IS THE REAL PRIZE: `task decisions:uncovered` reports a decision NO SLICE CARRIES, counting citations across entries so 0011's cli-catalog-member-gate is credited with 0010's D17, D21, D25 and D42. That is the audit 0010's own 2026-08-05 event describes doing BY HAND, which found seven pieces of decided work with no slice — D36's library half being real code whose absence would have shipped a schema whose matching read an emptied field. `task vet` checks every cited number resolves and refuses a decision both carried and listed unsliced; coverage itself is deliberately NOT a gate, since an entry's design is legitimately allowed to run ahead of its plan. THE CHECK PAID FOR ITSELF ON FIRST RUN, twice. It rejected the migration's own output — cli-catalog-member-gate's `(0010 D17, D21, D25, D42)` had been read as one cross-entry ref and three local ones, when 0011 D22 says in its own text that all four are 0010's. And it found two genuine gaps: D3 (the catalog's concrete version and the removed `0.0.0-dev` default) was implemented by core-identity-shape and cited by nothing, and D40's surviving identity-package half ships in 0011:core-identity-package and was likewise uncited. Both now carried. SEVEN DECISIONS ARE DELIBERATELY UNSLICED and say why, in a new top-level `unsliced` map: 0010's D2, D7, D16 and D23 (three reversed or superseded by D38, one a decision NOT to add a field) and 0011's D5, D10 and D14 (a reversed namespace half, a registry property gated on the ownerless Zot cutover, and a forward-looking reservation nobody publishes to). | [0013](./0013/) | cross-cutting | draft | - | not-started | 2026-07-27 — Design revised on review: D10 supersedes D1, D11 supersedes D4, D12 amends D9, and OQ1 is closed. D1 had removed the `#Secret` contract type AND the disjunction inside it, when only the routing metadata needed to move to the attribute — leaving the deployer no slot in which to say "this Secret already exists", and forcing the handle-plus-context-map machinery of D4 to compensate. D10 restores `#Secret` narrowed to `#SecretLiteral | #SecretRef`, so the ATTRIBUTE carries routing (author intent, static, in the published module) and the TYPE carries fulfilment (deployer choice, per environment, type-checked by CUE). D11 replaces handle substitution with resolve-in-place: the kernel rewrites every secret to its `#SecretRef` form, so both arms converge before render, a transformer reads two fields from one branch, and the whole handle format, the `#TransformerContext` addition, the `owned` flag and the output scanner are all deleted. Three properties fall out that the first draft lacked: instance files for supplied secrets do not change at all, plaintext in the render is structurally unrepresentable rather than stripped, and a secret interpolated into a rendered string fails at plain `cue vet` at authoring time. Experiment 02 rebuilt as `02-resolve-in-place` and re-run: all five claims held, and its Go content hash agrees with the CUE one in examples.cue. OQ2 opened — whether the arm rewrite survives the real kernel build path — and is now the sole blocker to acceptance. | Attribute-Declared Secret Fields |

| [0015](./0015/) | cross-cutting | draft | - | not-started | 2026-08-05 — Drafted from a design conversation grounded in three measurements taken the same day. `core/src/catalog.cue` carries exactly ONE member map, `#transformers`, and `library/opm/materialize/index.go:39-41` skips any catalog build without one — so a contract with no adapter is absent from the materialized world, which is precisely the state 0010 D37's `fulfilment: "provider"` creates on purpose. `compile/match.go:344-360` is SUBSET containment, not equality, so a more-specific transformer never displaces a less-specific one; both pair and both render, and 0010 D32's guard does not reach the case because it fires only for `fulfilment: "provider"` contracts. And the real discriminator across the 8 transformers sharing `catalog_opm`'s `#ContainerResource` bucket is `requiredLabels` (`daemonset_transformer.cue:27-29`), not the resource/trait set — which is what makes 0010 D36's `matchLabels` the lever for provider classes rather than a new matcher concept. Four decisions locked: D1 (explicit contract maps), D2 (classes, amending 0010 D37), D3 (RBAC-gated registration CR), D4 (no contract/adapter packaging split, decided now because riding 0010's FQN break is nearly free and a standalone break later is not). Six Open Questions carried. | Catalog Contracts, Provider Classes, and Transformer Registration |

## Status legend

- **draft** — initial design, actively being written
- **accepted** — design agreed upon, ready for implementation
- **implemented** — design has been realized in code
- **superseded** — replaced by a newer enhancement (see `superseded_by` in the entry's config.yaml)
